title: The Well and the Water Dispute (TE)
summary: A greedy neighbor sells a well to a farmer, then demands rent for the water. Birbal's famous verdict orders the cheat to remove his water immediately.
full_text:
A hardworking farmer named Ramu purchased a deep stone well from his wealthy neighbor, Seth Dhaniram, paying thirty gold coins before the village elders so he could irrigate his parched fields.

The next morning, when Ramu lowered his bucket to draw water, Dhaniram stopped him with a sneer: 'Halt, peasant! I sold you the well, but I never sold you the water inside it! The water remains my private property. If you draw even a single bucket, you must pay me five copper coins!'

Ramu wept in despair and brought his grievance to Emperor Akbar's court.

Akbar summoned Dhaniram, who presented his deed with smug confidence: 'Your Majesty, a contract is sacred. The deed explicitly states I transferred ownership of the stone structure. It does not mention water. The water is mine!'

Akbar looked at Birbal. Birbal stepped forward, bowed politely to the merchant, and said:

'Seth Dhaniram, your argument is flawless. You sold only the stone structure, so the well belongs entirely to Ramu, while the water belongs exclusively to you.'

Dhaniram grinned with triumph: 'Thank you, wise minister!'

'However,' Birbal continued with a sudden, razor-sharp smile, 'since the well belongs entirely to Ramu, you have no right to keep your water stored inside his property! You are trespassing!

'Therefore, the court orders: you must remove every single drop of your water from Ramu's well before sunset today! And for every day your water has occupied his well since the sale, you must pay Ramu a storage fee of fifty gold mohurs!'

Dhaniram turned pale as a ghost. To remove thousands of gallons of water within hours was impossible, and the storage fee would bankrupt him!

Dhaniram fell at Ramu's feet, begged for mercy, and surrendered all claims to the water forever. Akbar praised Birbal's peerless jurisprudence.
